findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security. The case-sensitive comparison lets an admin bypass the self-removal prohibition by uppercasing letters in their own account ID. The controller uses ParseUUIDPipe (members.controller.ts:19), which [accepts uppercase UUIDs and preserves their casing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nestjs/nest/v11.2.7/packages/common/pipes/parse-uuid.pipe.ts). This comparison then fails, while [PostgreSQL treats the uppercase UUID as the same identifier](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype-uuid.html), so the following queries remove the admin's own membership and sessions. A sole admin becomes locked out, and the retained-account policy prevents inviting them back. Normalize both identifiers before comparing and cover this request in the HTTP test.
Case: normal use - an authenticated admin sends their own UUID using uppercase hexadecimal letters.
findings.title: Canonicalize UUIDs before checking self-removal
